pages.text: Mass is the reactor's fuel. $(thing)Every block counts as 1 mass$(), whatever it is.$(br2)Insert blocks by hand, with hoppers, or with pipes.$(br2)Once it's running, you can also throw things into the ring: the black hole pulls in anything inside the ring's hole. It pulls on everything in a $(thing)sphere of influence$() that just fits inside the ring, the ground below included: blocks are torn loose a surface at a time, eating a bowl under the core. $(danger)In a failure the sphere grows$(): past the ring in a stall or fault, further in pre-meltdown and after a breach, and much further in a meltdown. Every item and every block is $(num)1$() mass, and a creature is $(num)1$() mass per heart. The mass is split evenly across the four stabilizers.$(br2)The more mass the reactor holds, the $(thing)bigger the black hole$() and the harder it pulls: four times the ignition minimum makes it twice as wide and pull twice as hard.

Each stabilizer needs at least $(num)10,000$() mass before ignition. There is $(thing)no maximum$().$(br2)More mass runs longer, but makes a bigger crater if it all goes wrong.$(br2)A comparator shows how close a port is to the ignition minimum.
